title: Coins bend logical circles; only isotropy makes them round
subject: Whether random parity laws have round circles
conclusion: When coins split each four-place knot of the square parity law into two three-place knots, distance in the plane dual is exactly the coordinate sum minus the longest strictly increasing chain of matching squares and bond distance is twice it at large scale, so the circle is a square with elliptic corners, quarter circles for fair coins (pi = 3.44120), whose flat lattice sides persist. A parity law on a Poisson-Voronoi tessellation, with no preferred direction, is exactly round.
